say: You give it a ray from $A$ and a length. It marks the point $B$ on the ray so that $|AB|$ is exactly that length.
The key idea: the compass holds the length. Set it against the ruler, then swing it from $A$ and the arc cuts the ray at the right distance.

how.ordinary: It shows up on Paper 2 as a step inside longer constructions, such as drawing a triangle or parallelogram with given side lengths, in 2016, 2018, 2022 and 2023.

example.question: Draw a ray starting at $A$. Construct the point $B$ on the ray so that $|AB| = 5$ cm.

steps.title: Set the compass
steps.say: Place the compass point on $0$ on the ruler. Open the pencil to $5$ cm.

lines.text: Do not change this setting until you have drawn the arc.

steps.title: Draw the arc
steps.say: Move the compass point to $A$. Swing the pencil so the arc crosses the ray.

lines.text: Leave the arc on the page. It is the construction line.

ordinary.tip: Marks are given for each correct element of the construction, so every length and arc you draw counts. Show them all.
Work on the diagram earns partial credit, so start the construction even if you are unsure of the rest.

say: You give it an angle. It draws the line that cuts the angle into two **equal** angles, using only a compass and a straight edge.
The key idea: two points the same distance from the vertex, then two equal arcs from those points. The arcs cross on the bisector.

how.ordinary: It appeared on Paper 2 in 2024 as part of a 30-mark question, where two angle bisectors were drawn to find the incircle of a triangle.

example.question: Draw an angle $\angle BAC$. Construct its bisector.

steps.title: Mark equal distances
steps.say: Put the compass point on $A$. Draw an arc that cuts both arms. Call the points $P$ and $Q$.

lines.text: Both points are the same distance from $A$.

steps.title: Draw two equal arcs
steps.say: Put the point on $P$ and draw an arc inside the angle. Keep the same setting, put the point on $Q$ and draw a second arc. Call the crossing $R$.

lines.text: Leave all arcs on the page.

steps.title: Draw the bisector
steps.say: With the straight edge, join $A$ to $R$ and extend it.

lines.text: Line $AR$ splits $\angle BAC$ into two equal angles.

ordinary.tip: Each bisector earns marks of its own, so draw every bisector asked for with its arcs showing.
When two bisectors are used to find the incircle, extend them until they meet. If they do not intersect, you lose a mark.

say: You give it a ray and a number of degrees. It draws a second arm from the end of the ray so the angle between them is exactly that size.
The key idea: the protractor does the measuring. Line up its centre and its zero, then mark the angle on the scale.

how.ordinary: It shows up on Paper 2 as a step inside longer constructions, such as drawing a triangle or parallelogram from given sides and angles, in 2016, 2018 and 2023.

example.question: Draw a ray $[AB]$. Construct the angle $\angle BAC = 50^\circ$.

steps.title: Place the protractor
steps.say: Put the centre of the protractor on $A$. Line its base up along the ray $AB$.

lines.text: The ray must pass through the $0^\circ$ mark.

steps.title: Mark the angle
steps.say: Read round from $0^\circ$ on the side the ray points to, until you reach $50^\circ$. Make a small dot there. Call it $C$.

lines.text: Check you used the scale that starts at $0^\circ$ on the ray.

steps.title: Draw the arm
steps.say: Remove the protractor. With the ruler, draw a line from $A$ through $C$.

ordinary.tip: Draw a labelled pilot diagram first. It earns marks even if the final construction goes wrong.
Label every vertex. A correct construction with the vertices not named or left out still loses marks.

say: You give it two side lengths. It builds a **rectangle** with those sides, with all four angles right angles.
The key idea: draw one side, build a right angle at each end, then measure the other side up each of them.

example.question: Construct the rectangle $ABCD$ with $|AB| = 6$ cm and $|BC| = 4$ cm.

steps.title: Draw the base
steps.say: Draw a line. Mark $A$. Set the compass to $6$ cm and mark $B$ on the line.

steps.title: Make right angles
steps.say: At $A$ and at $B$, use the protractor to draw a line at $90^\circ$ to $AB$, on the same side.

lines.text: Both lines go up from the base.

steps.title: Measure the height
steps.say: Set the compass to $4$ cm. With the point on $A$, mark $D$ on the upright line. With the point on $B$, mark $C$ on the other.

lines.text: Check that $|DC| = 6$ cm and the angles are $90^\circ$.
